q: 1. The most desirable alignment of an irrigation canal is along .............
explain: A ridge canal (watershed canal) is ideal because it allows gravity irrigation on both sides of the canal and avoids the need for cross-drainage works.

q: 2. The cone formula to compute the storage volume V between two contours with an elevation difference of h m is given by .............
explain: The Prismoidal (or Cone) formula is used to calculate the volume between two parallel areas A1 and A2 separated by a vertical distance h.

q: 3. Which of the following canal has the command area only on one side?
explain: Contour canals follow the contour of the land; because the ground on the uphill side is higher than the canal, irrigation is only possible on the downhill side.

q: 4. If V0 is the critical velocity, according to Kennedy's theory the silt supporting velocity of a canal is proportional to .............
explain: While the relationship is complex, empirical observations in the theory suggest the silt-carrying capacity is related to the velocity raised to a higher power (approx 2.5).

q: 5. The balanced depth of cutting of a canal is one in which .............
options: the volume of cutting is equal to the volume of embankment
the volume of cutting is less than the volume of embankment
there is no cutting but only embankment
there is only cutting and no embankment
explain: Balanced depth (or economical depth) is the specific depth of excavation where the earth removed from cutting exactly matches the amount needed to construct the banks (filling), minimizing cost.

q: 6. A spoil bank is formed when .............
options: the canal section is too large
the canal has steep bed slope
the volume of excavation is in excess of embankment filling
explain: When the earth excavated from the canal is more than what is required for the banks, the surplus soil is deposited in heaps parallel to the canal, called spoil banks.

q: 7. In non-modular outlet the discharge is affected by .............
options: the fluctuations both in the distributory and field channels
the fluctuations only in the field channel
is independent of fluctuations in the distribution and field channels
explain: Non-modular outlets (like a simple pipe) function like a submerged orifice; therefore, the discharge depends on the water level difference between the supply canal and the receiving field channel.

q: 8. Syphon well drop (or cylindrical fall) in the canals is provided when the discharge in the canal .............
options: is large and the drop is small
is large and the drop is also large
is small and the drop is also small
is small but the drop is large
explain: Syphon well drops are economical and efficient for small discharges (like in tail-end distributaries) combined with a high vertical drop.

q: 9. In the case of an aqueduct, if the canal section is flumed then it is called .............
explain: A Type III aqueduct involves fluming (narrowing) the canal section and providing concrete or masonry sides to reduce the overall cost of the structure across the drain.

q: 10. A canal meant to convey water from one source to the other is known as .............
explain: A link canal is used to connect two different rivers or systems (like the Indus-Jhelum link) to transfer surplus water to a water-deficient area.

q: 11. The weed growth in a canal leads to .............
explain: Weeds increase the roughness of the channel (n), which decreases the velocity and consequently reduces the discharge capacity (Q = AV).

q: 12. The shape of a lined canal recommended by ISI is .............
explain: The trapezoidal section with rounded corners is standard for large canals because it is hydraulically efficient and easier to construct with lining materials.

q: 13. The purpose of a cross regulator is .............
options: to increase the depth of flow u/s when the main canal is running with low flow
to regulate the flow in the distributaries
explain: A cross regulator is built across the main canal to 'head up' water. This ensures that even when the main canal has low discharge, the water level is high enough to feed an off-taking distributary canal.

q: 14. The proportion of silt in water is called .............
explain: Silt charge is the technical term for the concentration of suspended sediment in a stream, usually measured in parts per million (ppm) or grams per liter.

q: 15. In a homogeneous earth dam without d/s horizontal filter, portion of the d/s face through which seepage flow comes out is
options: neither a stream line nor an equipotential line
explain: The discharge face (seepage surface) on the downstream side is neither a flow line (streamline) nor a constant head line (equipotential line).

q: 16. A canal carries a discharge of 5 m³/s with a slope of 1/100. For the same depth of flow its discharge carrying capacity will be doubled by increasing its slope to
explain: According to Manning's formula, $V \propto \sqrt{S}$. To double the discharge ($Q=AV$), the velocity must double, meaning the slope must increase by $2^2 = 4$ times. $(1/100) \times 4 = 1/25$.

q: 17. The source from which the soil is obtained to make up for the difference between the soil required for embankment and the soil available from the canal excavation is known as
explain: When earthwork in cutting is less than earthwork in filling, the extra soil is dug from 'Borrow Pits'.

q: 18. The canal breach may occur when
options: piping takes place through the canal bank
canal banks are over-topped by excess flows
cultivator cut the embankment to derive additional supply
explain: Canal breaches (structural failures of the bank) can be caused by internal erosion (piping), overtopping, or human interference/intentional cuts.

q: 19. When the length of the body wall of the fall is less than the normal width of the canal, the fall is then called
explain: A fall is 'flumed' when the crest length is narrower than the canal's bed width, usually requiring transitions to prevent turbulence.

q: 20. The proportional weir is also called as
explain: A Sutro weir is a specially shaped weir where the discharge is directly proportional to the head ($Q \propto H$).

q: 21. If m is the average particle size of silt in mm, then the silt factor is proportional to
explain: Lacey's silt factor formula is $f = 1.76\sqrt{m}$, where $m$ is the particle size in mm.

q: 22. A contour canal
options: is most suitable is hilly areas
is aligned parallel to the contour of the country
explain: Contour canals are common in hills; since they follow the terrain elevation, they can only deliver water to the side that is lower in elevation.

q: 23. The narrow strip of land left at the ground level between the inner toe of the bank and top edge of the cutting, is known as
explain: Berms act as a buffer to prevent bank erosion and provide space for future widening of the canal.

q: 24. The height of dowel above the road level should not be more than
explain: A dowel is a small curb on the canal bank road to prevent vehicles from falling; 30 cm is the standard maximum height.

q: 25. The width of dowel is, usually, kept from
explain: Dowels typically range from 0.3 to 0.6 meters in width to remain stable and functional as a safety curb.

q: 26. The sodium carbonate lining consists of at least
explain: A low-cost lining method involves mixing approximately 1% sodium carbonate with 6% clay into the soil to reduce permeability.

q: 27. The weed growth in a canal leads to
explain: Weeds increase the rugosity (roughness) of the channel, which slows down the water velocity and reduces the overall discharge capacity.

q: 28. A channel is said to be in scouring when the critical velocity ratio is ............. one.
explain: If the CVR ($m$) is greater than 1, the actual velocity is higher than the critical velocity required to prevent scouring, leading to bed erosion.

q: 29. The main cause of silting in channel is
explain: Silting occurs when velocity drops (due to poor slope or design) or when excessive silt enters through the head regulator.

q: 30. The channel after attaining its section and longitudinal slope, will be said to be in ............. regime.
explain: Final regime is the state reached when a channel has adjusted its perimeter, depth, and slope to become stable in alluvium.

q: 31. Distributary head regulators are provided
options: to control the supplies to the off-taking channel
to control the silt entry in the off-taking canal
to stop the supply, when not needed, in the off-taking canal
explain: These regulators act as valves to manage discharge, sediment intake, and closure for the smaller off-taking canal.

q: 32. A structure constructed in an irrigation canal for the purpose of wasting some of its water, is known as a
explain: Escapes act as safety valves to discharge excess water caused by heavy rain or sudden closures of off-takes.

q: 33. The cylinder or well fall is quite suitable and economical for
explain: Well falls are ideal for dropping small amounts of water over high vertical distances, such as in hilly terrain.

q: 34. The discharge (Q) over trapezoidal crest of Sarda fall is ............. as compared to rectangular crest of identical parameters.
explain: Due to the wider side area in a trapezoidal shape, the discharge capacity is slightly higher than a rectangular crest of the same base width.

q: 35. The fall which can be used as meter fall, is
explain: A flumed glacis fall can be calibrated to accurately measure the discharge passing through it.

q: 36. An outlet in which the discharge depends upon the difference in level between the water levels in distributing channel and the water course, is known as
explain: Non-modular outlets (like a simple pipe) vary their discharge based on the water levels of both the parent canal and the field channel.

q: 37. A diversion head work is constructed to .............
options: raise water level at the head of the canal
regulate the intake of water into the canal
reduce fluctuations in the supply level of the river
explain: Diversion head works serve multiple purposes: raising water level for gravity flow, regulating intake, and controlling silt and river fluctuations.

q: 38. A weir is generally aligned at right angle to the direction of the main river flow because .............
options: less length of weir is required
explain: A perpendicular alignment is the most efficient and economical way to span a river, providing the shortest length and uniform discharge across the crest.

q: 39. According to Khosla's theory, the undermining of the floor starts from the .............
explain: Undermining or piping starts from the downstream (tail) end where the exit gradient is highest and water emerges from the soil.

q: 40. A hydraulic jump is formed when .............
options: a sub-critical flow strikes against a super-critical flow
a super-critical flow strikes against a sub-critical flow
the two flows of super-critical velocity meet each other
the two flows of sub-critical velocity meet each other
explain: A hydraulic jump occurs when rapid, super-critical flow transitions to a slower, sub-critical flow state, resulting in energy dissipation.

q: 41. For low navigation dams, the type of gate used is .............
explain: Bear trap gates are often used in navigation because they can be lowered completely to allow vessels to pass over them.

q: 42. The crest level in a barrage is kept at a ............. level.
explain: As noted in 317, the physical crest of a barrage is kept low to prevent significant obstruction during high floods.

q: 43. The crest of the under-sluices should be lower than the crest of the head regulator (if silt excluder is provided) by at least .............
explain: The under-sluice pocket is kept lower (usually 1.0 to 1.2m) to create a 'still pond' which helps in settling silt before water enters the canal.

q: 44. When the bed level of the canal is higher than the highest flood level (H.F.L.) of the drainage, then the cross drainage work is said to be .............
explain: In a simple aqueduct, the canal passes over the drainage with enough clearance that the drainage water never touches the canal bottom.

q: 45. When the levels are such that the F.S.L. of the canal is much above the bed level of the drainage trough, so that the canal runs under syphonic action under the trough, the structure provided is known as .............
explain: When the drainage HFL is higher than the canal bed and the canal is forced to dip under the drainage trough, it is a siphon aqueduct.

q: 46. In case of siphon aqueduct, the H.F.L. of the drain is .............
options: much below the bottom of the canal trough
much higher above the canal bed
in level with the canal bed
explain: For syphonic action to occur in the drainage water passing under a canal, the drainage HFL must be higher than the canal bed (or underside of the trough).

q: 47. In a super-passage, the F.S.L. of the canal is .............
options: lower than the underside of the trough carrying drainage water
above the bed level of the drainage trough
in level with the drainage trough
explain: In a super-passage, the canal flow is at atmospheric pressure and its Full Supply Level (FSL) must remain below the bottom of the drainage trough.

q: 48. If water table is comparatively high, the irrigation canal becomes useless, due to .............
options: water logging of the cultivated areas
explain: When the water table is high, additional irrigation leads to waterlogging (saturation of the root zone), which prevents aeration and destroys crop productivity.

q: 49. A counter berm is .............
options: a horizontal benching provided on the inside slope
a horizontal benching provided on the outside slope
a vertical benching provided on the outer edge of the bank
a vertical benching provided on the inner edge of the bank
explain: A counter berm is added to the outside of a canal bank to keep the saturation line well within the body of the bank, preventing leaks.

q: 50. A minimum of 90 cm free board is provided if the discharge in the canal is between .............
explain: Freeboard increases with discharge capacity. For large canals (>60 cumecs), 90 cm (0.9m) is standard.

q: 51. If straight sides of a triangular section of a lined canal with circular bottom of radius R, make an angle θ with horizontal, the area of its cross-section, is .............
explain: Based on the geometric properties of a standard triangular canal section with a rounded bottom, the area $A = R^2 (\theta + \cot \theta)$.

q: 52. The main function of a diversion head works of canal from a river, is .............
explain: The primary role is to raise the river's water level (pond level) so that water can flow into the off-taking canal by gravity.

q: 53. The crest level of a canal diversion head work, depends upon .............
explain: The crest level of the weir is dictated by the required pond level needed to feed the canal at its Full Supply Level.

q: 54. The length of a meander is the distance along the river between the tangent point of one curve to the tangent point of .............
options: next curve of the same order
reverse curve plus the width of the river
explain: Meander length is measured as the axial distance between two corresponding points (like consecutive crests) on the same side of the meander.

q: 55. A river is said to be of .............
options: aggrading type if it builds up its bed
degrading type if it cuts its bed
meandering type if it flows in sinuous curve
explain: These are the three primary morphological classifications of alluvial rivers based on their bed-level trends and planform.
